title: What is an Article?
content: Articles are a type of determiner that come before nouns. English has three articles: 'a', 'an', and 'the'. They tell us whether we are talking about a specific thing or a general one.

title: Indefinite Articles: A and An
content: Use 'a' and 'an' when referring to something non-specific or mentioned for the first time. Use 'a' before words that start with a consonant sound: a car, a book, a university (note: 'university' starts with a 'y' sound). Use 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound: an apple, an elephant, an hour (note: 'hour' starts with a silent 'h', so it takes 'an').

title: The Definite Article: The
content: Use 'the' when referring to something specific that both the speaker and listener already know about. Examples: 'Please close the door behind you' (a specific door). 'The sun is shining' (there is only one sun). 'Can you pass me the salt?' (the salt on this table). 'The' can be used before both singular and plural nouns.

title: When NOT to Use an Article
content: Articles are not used before: proper nouns (Paris, Microsoft), most country names (France, Brazil), uncountable nouns used in general (Water is important), plural nouns used in general (Dogs are loyal), and languages or subjects (She studies English, He teaches math).
